question.r:
**Ask Better Questions:** Include clear details about your problem: what you're trying to do, what you expected, what actually happened, and any relevant code or errors. This makes it much easier for others to help you.
https://stackoverflow.com/help/how-to-ask

**Don't Ask to Ask:** Instead of asking if you can ask a question, just ask it directly. This helps others understand your issue right away.
https://dontasktoask.com/

**Avoid Images of Errors:** Please copy and paste the error message as text using code blocks. This makes it easier to read, search, and debug.
https://idownvotedbecau.se/imageofatextualerror/

**Avoid Images of Code:** Share code as text in code blocks so others can read, copy, and test it. Images make this difficult.
https://idownvotedbecau.se/imageofcode/

**"It's Not Working" Isn't Enough:** Explain what you expected, what actually happened, and include relevant code or errors. More detail leads to better help.
http://idownvotedbecau.se/itsnotworking/

**Provide a Minimal Reproducible Example:** Share the smallest amount of code needed to reproduce your issue so others can quickly understand and test it.
https://stackoverflow.com/help/minimal-reproducible-example

**Show Your Attempt:** Include what you've already tried. This helps others understand where you're stuck and avoids repeating suggestions.
http://idownvotedbecau.se/noattempt/

**No Code Provided:** It's difficult to help without seeing the relevant code. Please include the parts related to your issue.
http://idownvotedbecau.se/nocode/

**Try Debugging First:** Read error messages, add logs, and test parts of your code to narrow down the issue. Sharing your debugging steps helps others assist you.
http://idownvotedbecau.se/nodebugging/

**Include the Error Message:** If your code produces an error, share the full message. It often contains important clues.
http://idownvotedbecau.se/noerror/

**Don't Just Say Hello:** Ask your question directly instead of starting with only a greeting. This helps others respond more efficiently.
https://www.nohello.net/

**Do Some Research First:** Try searching or checking documentation before asking. If you still need help, mention what you've already looked at.
http://idownvotedbecau.se/noresearch/
**Ask Directly:** Briefly describe your actual problem instead of asking if someone knows about a topic. This makes it easier to help right away.
**Keep It Concise:** Your message is quite long. Try summarizing the key points so others can understand your issue quickly.

**Too Much Code:** Avoid sharing entire projects. Focus on the smallest portion of code that reproduces the issue.
http://idownvotedbecau.se/toomuchcode/
**Too Much Information:** Remove unrelated details and focus on what is directly relevant to your problem.

**Community Guidelines:** https://discord.com/guidelines
**Terms of Service:** https://discord.com/terms
**Try It Yourself:** Experiment with your code or idea first. Testing things on your own is often the fastest way to learn and understand the issue.

**Unclear Question:** Please clarify what you're trying to do, include relevant code, and explain the issue more clearly.
http://idownvotedbecau.se/unclearquestion/

**The XY Problem:** You're asking about a specific solution instead of the actual problem. Explain your original goal so better solutions can be suggested.
https://xyproblem.info/

rules.r: **No Backseat Coding:** Avoid giving unsolicited advice or taking over someone else's troubleshooting unless they ask for it. It can confuse the person being helped and disrupt the flow of the conversation.
**One Topic at a Time:** Avoid switching topics while someone is helping you with an issue. This makes it difficult to follow progress. Once your issue is resolved, you can start a new discussion.

**AI Usage:** AI tools can be helpful, but they may produce outdated or incorrect code. If you are sharing AI-generated code, please mention it. Make sure you understand what you are posting so others can help effectively.

**No Cheating:** Do not ask for help with graded assignments, interviews, or anything that involves academic or professional dishonesty. This community is here to help you learn, not to bypass the process.
**Crypto Policy:** This server does not provide support for cryptocurrency, NFTs, or blockchain-related projects. Please use communities dedicated to those topics.
**No Direct Messages for Help:** Keep help-related discussions in public channels. This allows others to learn and ensures multiple people can assist if needed.
**English Only:** Please use English in this channel so moderators and members can understand and assist you effectively.
**No Help with Active Exams:** Requests related to ongoing exams, certifications, or timed tests are not allowed.
**No Flaming or Toxicity:** Be respectful. Personal attacks, insults, or aggressive behavior are not allowed. Keep discussions constructive.
**No Requests for Free Work:** Do not ask others to build projects or features for you. Show your own work and ask for guidance instead.
**No Hacking or Exploits:** Do not discuss or request help with unauthorized access, exploits, or malicious activities.
**Use Images Appropriately:** Avoid excessive or unnecessary images. For code or errors, use text and code blocks instead of screenshots.
**Move On:** This discussion is no longer productive. Please stop and move to another topic.
**Nickname Policy:** Use a readable and appropriate nickname. Avoid names that are hard to mention, misleading, or disruptive.
**No Unnecessary Pings:** Do not ping users or staff for general help. Ask your question normally and wait for a response.
**Scraping Policy:** Make sure your automation follows the target site's rules. Do not ask for help bypassing protections or scraping restricted platforms like Discord.
**No Self-Bots:** Automating a user account violates Discord's Terms of Service. Discussion or support for self-bots is not allowed.
**No Spoon-Feeding:** Focus on learning rather than copying solutions. Try to understand the guidance you receive.
**Voice Channel Rules:** Keep your microphone clear and avoid disruptive noise. Be respectful and do not interrupt or disturb ongoing conversations.
